items.title: 14.2.5 Dot Product of Vectors in terms of their components (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Ab tak dot product ki do definitions aayin: angle wali aur components wali. Is sabaq mein hum dekhenge ke space mein components wala formula asal mein kahan se aata hai. Iske liye do cheezein chahiye jo hum seekh chuke hain: distributive property (14.2.4) aur unit vectors ki table (14.2.2). Phir teen khoobsurat examples aayenge jin mein dot product trigonometry ke mashhoor formulas saabit karta hai.

Farz karein \(\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}\) aur \(\underline{v} = a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k}\) do non-zero vectors hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab mein dono vectors ka beech wala term \(b_{1}\underline{i}\) aur \(b_{2}\underline{i}\) chhapa hai. Sahi \(b_{1}\underline{j}\) aur \(b_{2}\underline{j}\) hai:
\[\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{v} = a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k}\]
Aage ka hisaab kitab bhi \(\underline{j}\) ke saath hi karti hai.

Distributive law se hum likh sakte hain:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k})\]
\[\cdot\ (a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k})\]
\[= a_{1}a_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}) + a_{1}b_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j})\]
\[+ a_{1}c_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{k}) + b_{1}a_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{i})\]
\[+ b_{1}b_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{j}) + b_{1}c_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{k})\]
\[+ c_{1}a_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{i}) + c_{1}b_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{j})\]
\[+ c_{1}c_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{k})\]

\[\Rightarrow \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\]
because
\[\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = \underline{j} \cdot \underline{j} = \underline{k} \cdot \underline{k} = 1\]
\[\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = \underline{j} \cdot \underline{k} = \underline{k} \cdot \underline{i} = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kyun: brackets kholne se \(3 \times 3 = 9\) terms bante hain, bilkul jaise \((x + y + z)(p + q + r)\) mein. Ab 14.2.2 ki table lagayein: jin chhe (6) terms mein do alag unit vectors hain (jaise \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j}\)), woh zero ho jate hain. Jin teen terms mein ek hi unit vector do dafa hai (\(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}\), \(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{j}\), \(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{k}\)), un ki value \(1\) hai, is liye sirf coefficient bachta hai. Isi liye aakhir mein sirf \(a_{1}a_{2}\), \(b_{1}b_{2}\), \(c_{1}c_{2}\) bache.
Is liye do vectors ka dot product un ke corresponding (aamne saamne wale) components ke products ka jor hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \((2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}) \cdot (\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + 2\underline{k})\):
\[= (2)(1) + (-1)(4) + (3)(2)\]
\[= 2 - 4 + 6 = 4\]
Teen products, phir jor. Har product bracket mein likhne se sign ki ghalti nahin hoti.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Show that the components of a vector are the projections of that vector along \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) and \(\underline{k}\) respectively.
steps:
Given: ek vector \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\).
To prove: \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\), \(\underline{k}\) ke saath is ki projections \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) hain.
Method: 14.2.3 wala formula lagayenge: \(\underline{u}\) ke saath \(\underline{v}\) ki projection \(= \frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\). Yahan \(\underline{u}\) ki jagah baari baari \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\), \(\underline{k}\) aayenge, aur in sab ki lambai \(1\) hai, is liye divide karna aasan hai.

Step 1: \(\underline{i}\) ke saath projection
\[\dfrac{\underline{v} \cdot \underline{i}}{|\underline{i}|} = (a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}) \cdot \underline{i}\]
\[= a(1) + b(0) + c(0) = a\]
Kyun: \(|\underline{i}| = 1\), aur 14.2.2 ki table se \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 1\), \(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{i} = 0\), \(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{i} = 0\). Teen terms mein se sirf ek bachta hai.

Step 2: \(\underline{j}\) ke saath projection
\[\dfrac{\underline{v} \cdot \underline{j}}{|\underline{j}|} = (a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}) \cdot \underline{j} = b\]
Kyun: ab sirf \(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{j} = 1\) bachta hai; baqi dono zero.

Step 3: \(\underline{k}\) ke saath projection
\[\dfrac{\underline{v} \cdot \underline{k}}{|\underline{k}|} = (a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}) \cdot \underline{k} = c\]
Kyun: sirf \(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{k} = 1\) bachta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(\underline{v} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) lein: \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{i} = 2\), \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{j} = -3\), \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{k} = 5\). Bilkul is ke components!
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\underline{v} = a\underline{i} + b\underline{j} + c\underline{k}\) ke components \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) hi \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\), \(\underline{k}\) ke saath \(\underline{v}\) ki projections hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 6 components ka asal matlab samjhata hai: \(a\) batata hai ke \(\underline{v}\) \(x\)-axis ki simt mein kitna phaila hai, \(b\) \(y\)-axis ki simt mein, aur \(c\) \(z\)-axis ki simt mein. Yani components hi teeno axes par vector ke saaye hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar kisi vector ka \(\underline{k}\) wala component zero ho, jaise \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} + 4\underline{j}\), to \(z\)-axis par us ka saya kitna hoga? Jawab: \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{k} = 0\), yani koi saya nahin. Iska matlab hai ke yeh vector poori tarah \(xy\)-plane mein para hai aur \(z\)-axis ke bilkul perpendicular hai. Dekha, ek chhota sa dot product humein vector ki jagah ke baare mein kitna kuch bata deta hai.
Ab ek aisa example jo dikhata hai ke vectors geometry ke purane theorems ko kitni aasani se saabit karte hain.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem:
Prove that in any triangle \(ABC\)
(i) \(a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc\cos A\) (Cosine Law)
(ii) \(a = b\cos C + c\cos B\) (Projection Law)
steps:
Given: triangle \(ABC\), jis ki sides ki lambaiyan \(a = BC\), \(b = CA\), \(c = AB\) hain.
To prove: (i) cosine law, (ii) projection law.
Method: sides ke saath vectors \(\underline{a}\), \(\underline{b}\), \(\underline{c}\) lete hain: \(\underline{a}\) \(B\) se \(C\), \(\underline{b}\) \(C\) se \(A\), \(\underline{c}\) \(A\) se \(B\) (triangle ke gird ek chakkar, figures dekhiye). Phir \(\underline{a} + \underline{b} + \underline{c} = \underline{0}\). Is equation ka munasib vectors ke saath dot product le kar \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) lagayenge. Yahan sab se ahem kaam sahi angle pehchanna hai.

Step 1: Vectors triangle ko band karte hain
\[\underline{a} + \underline{b} + \underline{c} = \underline{0}\]
Kyun: \(B\) se \(C\), phir \(C\) se \(A\), phir \(A\) se wapas \(B\): hum wahin aa gaye jahan se chale the, is liye kul displacement (jagah ki tabdeeli) zero hai. Jaise ghar se dukaan, dukaan se school, school se wapas ghar: aakhir mein aap ghar par hi hain.

(i) Step 2: \(\underline{a}\) ko alag karein
\[\underline{a} = -(\underline{b} + \underline{c})\]
Kyun: humein \(a^{2} = \underline{a} \cdot \underline{a}\) chahiye, \(b\) aur \(c\) ki shakal mein. Is liye \(\underline{a}\) ko ek taraf akela kar liya.

(i) Step 3: Dono taraf ka apne aap se dot product
\[\underline{a} \cdot \underline{a} = (\underline{b} + \underline{c}) \cdot (\underline{b} + \underline{c})\]
\[= \underline{b} \cdot \underline{b} + \underline{b} \cdot \underline{c} + \underline{c} \cdot \underline{b} + \underline{c} \cdot \underline{c}\]
Kyun: \((-1)(-1) = 1\), is liye minus khatam. Distributive property se bracket bilkul algebra ki tarah khulti hai, jaise \((x + y)^{2}\).

(i) Step 4: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{u} = |\underline{u}|^{2}\) aur commutative property
\[a^{2} = b^{2} + 2\underline{b} \cdot \underline{c} + c^{2}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{a} \cdot \underline{a} = a^{2}\), \(\underline{b} \cdot \underline{b} = b^{2}\), \(\underline{c} \cdot \underline{c} = c^{2}\). Aur \(\underline{b} \cdot \underline{c} = \underline{c} \cdot \underline{b}\), is liye beech wale do terms mil kar \(2\underline{b} \cdot \underline{c}\) ban gaye.

(i) Step 5: \(\underline{b}\) aur \(\underline{c}\) ke darmiyan angle
\[\underline{b} \cdot \underline{c} = bc\cos(\pi - A)\]
\[a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} + 2bc\cos(\pi - A)\]
Kyun: yeh sab se nazuk qadam hai. \(\underline{b}\) point \(A\) par khatam hota hai aur \(\underline{c}\) point \(A\) se shuru hota hai, yani yeh head to tail hain. Angle naapne ke liye dono ki dum milani parti hai: \(\underline{b}\) ko \(A\) se aage barha dein (pehli figure ki dashed line). Ab \(\underline{c}\) aur is extension ke darmiyan angle triangle ka andar wala angle \(A\) nahin, balke bahar wala angle \(\pi - A\) hai.

(i) Step 6: \(\cos(\pi - A) = -\cos A\) lagayein
\[a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc\cos A\]
Kyun: allied angles ka qaida: \(\pi - A\) doosre quadrant mein hai jahan cosine negative hota hai. Plus ka sign minus mein badal gaya, aur cosine law mil gaya.

(ii) Step 7: \(\underline{a}\) ko doosri tarah likhein
\[\underline{a} = -\underline{b} - \underline{c}\]
Kyun: wahi band hone wali equation. Is dafa right side par \(\underline{a}\) ke saath dot product lenge, taa ke \(\cos B\) aur \(\cos C\) aa jayein.

(ii) Step 8: \(\underline{a}\) ke saath dot product
\[\underline{a} \cdot \underline{a} = -\underline{a} \cdot \underline{b} - \underline{a} \cdot \underline{c}\]
Kyun: equation ke dono taraf ek hi vector se dot product lene se barabari qaim rehti hai.

(ii) Step 9: Angles pehchanein
\[= -ab\cos(\pi - C) - ac\cos(\pi - B)\]
Kyun: \(\underline{a}\) point \(C\) par khatam aur \(\underline{b}\) wahin se shuru hota hai; dum milane par bahar wala angle \(\pi - C\) banta hai. Isi tarah \(\underline{c}\) point \(B\) par khatam aur \(\underline{a}\) wahin se shuru, is liye angle \(\pi - B\) (doosri figure).
Dhyan dein: kitab ki is line mein minus ke nishan scan mein bohat halke hain; sahi line yahi hai jo yahan likhi hai.

(ii) Step 10: Signs saaf karein
\[= -ab(-\cos C) - ac(-\cos B)\]
\[a^{2} = ab\cos C + ac\cos B\]
Kyun: \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\), aur minus guna minus plus hota hai.

(ii) Step 11: \(a\) se divide karein
\[a = b\cos C + c\cos B\]
Kyun: \(a\) side ki lambai hai, is liye zero nahin; is se divide karna jaaiz hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ek jaana pehchana right triangle lete hain: \(a = 5\), \(b = 4\), \(c = 3\) (right angle \(A\) par). To \(\cos A = 0\), \(\cos B = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos C = \frac{4}{5}\).
\[b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc\cos A = 16 + 9 - 0 = 25 = a^{2}\]
\[b\cos C + c\cos B = \tfrac{16}{5} + \tfrac{9}{5} = 5 = a\]
Dono laws sahi nikle.
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: (i) \(a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc\cos A\) aur (ii) \(a = b\cos C + c\cos B\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 7 ki chaabi (key) angle pehchanna hai. Do vectors ke darmiyan angle hamesha tail to tail naapa jata hai. Jab ek vector kisi kone (vertex) par khatam ho aur agla wahin se shuru ho, to pehle wale ko kone se aage barha dein. Ab dono ke darmiyan angle bahar wala angle hai: \(\pi - (\text{andar wala angle})\). Har \(\pi - A\), \(\pi - B\), \(\pi - C\) yahin se aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar Step 5 mein ghalti se \(\underline{b} \cdot \underline{c} = bc\cos A\) likh dete to kya hota? Jawab: \(a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} + 2bc\cos A\) aata, yani sign ulta. Right triangle (\(A = 90^{\circ}\)) mein dono se Pythagoras mil jata, is liye ghalti pakri nahin jaati; lekin \(A = 60^{\circ}\) wale equilateral triangle mein \(a^{2} = a^{2} + a^{2} + a^{2}\) aata, jo bilkul ghalat hai. Is liye angle hamesha tail to tail naapiye.

blocks.title: Example 8
steps:
Given: do angles \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) (\(\alpha > \beta\) lein).
To prove: \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\).
Method: yeh trigonometry ka mashhoor formula hai jo Unit 10 mein lambi geometry se saabit hua tha. Dot product se yeh chand lines mein saabit hota hai: do unit vectors lein jo \(x\)-axis ke saath \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) angle banayein, aur un ka dot product do tareeqon se nikaalein: angle se aur components se. Dono jawab barabar honge.

Step 1: Do unit vectors
\(\overrightarrow{OA}\) aur \(\overrightarrow{OB}\) \(xy\)-plane mein unit vectors hain jo positive \(x\)-axis ke saath \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) angle banate hain; is liye \(\angle AOB = \alpha - \beta\).
\[\overrightarrow{OA} = \cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{j}\]
\[\overrightarrow{OB} = \cos\beta\,\underline{i} + \sin\beta\,\underline{j}\]
Kyun: \(1\) lambai ka vector jo angle \(\alpha\) par ho, us ka \(x\)-component \(\cos\alpha\) aur \(y\)-component \(\sin\alpha\) hota hai. Yeh cosine aur sine ki definition hi hai (unit circle).

Step 2: Components se dot product
\[\overrightarrow{OA} \cdot \overrightarrow{OB}\]
\[= (\cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{j}) \cdot (\cos\beta\,\underline{i} + \sin\beta\,\underline{j})\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Kyun: matching components multiply kar ke jama (14.2.5).

Step 3: Angle se dot product
\[\overrightarrow{OA} \cdot \overrightarrow{OB} = |\overrightarrow{OA}||\overrightarrow{OB}|\cos(\alpha - \beta)\]
\[= \cos(\alpha - \beta)\]
Kyun: dono vectors ke darmiyan angle \(\alpha - \beta\) hai, aur dono ki lambai \(1\) hai, is liye sirf cosine bachta hai.

Step 4: Dono ko barabar karein
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Kyun: ek hi dot product ke do roop (shakal) hain, is liye barabar hone hi chahiye.

Tasdeeq:
\(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 30^{\circ}\):
\[\cos 30^{\circ} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[\cos 60^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} + \sin 60^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} + \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Dono taraf barabar.

blocks.caption: Figure: Example 8, unit vectors OA and OB with ∠AOB = α − β (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\): matching components multiply kar ke jama.
2. Vector ke components hi \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\), \(\underline{k}\) ke saath us ki projections hain (Example 6).
3. Dot product se cosine law, projection law (Example 7) aur \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) (Example 8) saabit hote hain.
4. Triangle ke gird ek doosre ke peeche chalne wale vectors ka angle bahar wala angle hota hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ghalat components multiply karna (jaise \(a_{1}b_{2}\)). Aise terms \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = 0\) ki wajah se khatam ho jate hain.
2. Head to tail vectors ke liye andar wala angle \(A\) le lena; is se sign ulat jata hai.
3. \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\) bhool jana.
4. Example 8 mein angle \(\alpha + \beta\) le lena. Dono vectors \(x\)-axis se naape gaye hain, is liye un ke darmiyan farq \(\alpha - \beta\) hai.
